title: Tests discard json.Unmarshal errors
evidence: handlers_test.go:77, handlers_test.go:121, handlers_test.go:123, handlers_test.go:125, handlers_test.go:142 call json.Unmarshal(data, &x) without checking the returned error
suggestion: Check the error (t.Fatal on failure) so a non-JSON response fails with a clear message instead of a misleading zero-value comparison

title: README states Go 1.22+ but go.mod requires go 1.26.6
evidence: README.md:9 says 'Go 1.22 or newer'; go.mod:3 declares 'go 1.26.6'
suggestion: Align the README prerequisite with the go directive, or lower the go directive to 1.22 (the oldest release with method+pattern ServeMux routing)

title: Oversized request body is reported as 400 invalid JSON rather than 413
evidence: handlers.go:52 wraps r.Body in io.LimitReader(r.Body, maxBodyBytes), which silently truncates; the truncated decode fails at handlers.go:54-55 as 'invalid JSON body'
suggestion: Use http.MaxBytesReader and map *http.MaxBytesError to 413 Request Entity Too Large

title: Statement coverage is 76%; main() and error branches are not exercised
evidence: scores.json test_coverage=0.76; main.go:11-33 (getenv, main) and the serverError paths at handlers.go:44-47, 98-100, 108-110 have no test in handlers_test.go
suggestion: Optional: add a store-failure test (closed DB) to cover the 500 and /health 503 branches

title: Beyond spec: strict body decoding, Location header, DB-backed health check, year validation
